# Both branches add the SAME secret path with no common ancestor. git invokes the
# secret driver with an empty base (%O); it must treat that as an empty base and do
# a real 2-way merge, not fail trying to decrypt a 0-byte file.

sesam-repo

# OURS adds config.env.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sh -c 'printf "shared=OURS\n" > config.env'
exec sesam add config.env --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours adds config.env'

# THEIRS, branched from before the add, adds the same path with different content.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sh -c 'printf "shared=THEIRS\n" > config.env'
exec sesam add config.env --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs adds config.env'

# Merge: add/add -> empty base. A real content merge (with markers), not a decrypt error.
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
! stderr 'signature footer'
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file config.env; 1 conflict'
grep '^<<<<<<< ' config.env
grep 'shared=OURS' config.env
grep 'shared=THEIRS' config.env

# Resolve and finalize.
exec sh -c 'printf "shared=RESOLVED\n" > config.env'
exec git add -A
exec git commit --no-edit
exec sesam verify
! grep '^<<<<<<< ' config.env
